subject.title: fix(openrouter): apply request policy to music generation requests

question: Should OpenRouter music-generation requests honor the same explicit models.providers.openrouter.request policy—including allowPrivateNetwork—as the other model-provider HTTP request surfaces?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound and the documented contract supports consistent policy inheritance, but removing the existing path-specific hard denial intentionally expands the scope of a security-sensitive operator opt-in and should be confirmed by the shared policy owner.

options.title: Confirm full policy inheritance
options.body: Merge the current design so music generation receives the canonical sanitized request policy while private-network access remains disabled unless the operator explicitly opts in.

options.title: Keep music private-network strict
options.body: Continue forwarding safe request settings but explicitly exclude allowPrivateNetwork for music, documenting and testing why this capability is intentionally narrower than other provider HTTP surfaces.

recommendation.title: Confirm full policy inheritance
recommendation.body: Merge the current design so music generation receives the canonical sanitized request policy while private-network access remains disabled unless the operator explicitly opts in.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared transport-policy refactor is the closest concrete ownership signal for deciding whether all provider HTTP capability consumers should inherit the same policy.
